Parth Prateem Sahu, Judge Order On Board 08/08/2023
1.

This petition has been filed by the petitioner seeking following reliefs:
"10.1.

That, this Hon'ble Court may be kind enough in issuing a writ in the nature of mandamus, certiorari or likewise any other appropriate writ, commanding and directing the respondents to produce the complete records relating to the case of the petitioner.

10.2. That, this Hon'ble Court may be kind enough in issuing a writ in the nature of mandamus, certiorari or likewise and other appropriate writ, commanding and directing the respondent No.01, Collector, Raigarh, District- Raigarh (CG) to refer the application of petitioner dated 26.04.2018, under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 before the appropriate authority (i.e.
Presiding Officer, Chhattisgarh Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority, Raipur (CG) with immediate effect/delay.

sentences.text: Any other relief, which the Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper looking to the facts and circumstance of the case, may also be granted."
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner was owner of the land bearing kh.
No.45 admeasuring 1.619 hectare situated at Village- Pandripani, Tahsil and District- Raigarh
. Out of the aforementioned land, 0.809 hectare of land was acquired for establishing NTPC Taliapali Coal Mining Project, Gharghoda, District- Raigarh.
Land acquisition proceedings was initiated in the year 2015 and award was passed on 09.12.2016.

Acquisition proceedings was without notice to the affected parties and after getting knowledge of the acquisition proceedings, the petitioner after collecting relevant documents has submitted an application under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short "the Act of 2013") raising an objection with regard to quantum of compensation.

sentences.text:
Application under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 submitted by the petitioner is not referred till date and, therefore, a direction be issued to respondent No.1 to refer the application under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 for consideration.
3. Learned counsel for the State submits that he may be granted further two weeks time to file reply.
4.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and also perused the documents annexed along with writ petition.
5. Along with writ petition, petitioner has placed on record copy of award dated 09.12.2016 passed by respondent No.2 in land acquisition Case No.51/A-82/2014-15.
Name of the petitioner in the award is mentioned as respondent No.7.
Petitioner has also enclosed copy of application under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 filed before respondent No.1.

Relevant provision under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 is extracted below for ready reference:-
"64. Reference to Authority -(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Authority, as the case may be,
whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the person to whom it is payable, the rights of Rehabilitation and Resettlement under Chapters V and VI or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested:

Provided that the Collector shall, within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of application, make a reference to the appropriate Authority:
Provided further that where the Collector fails to make such reference within the period so specified, the applicant may apply to the Authority, as the case may be,
requesting it to direct the Collector to make the reference to it within a period of thirty days.
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:

2

entities.text: Bajrang Lal Agrawal vs The State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Provided further that the Collector may entertain an application after the expiry of the said period, within a further period of one year, if he is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing it within the period specified in the first proviso."

6. Perusal of the aforementioned provision would show that it mandates the Collector to make reference to the appropriate authority within the period of thirty days from the date of receipt of application.

Learned counsel for petitioner has submitted that the reference application under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 has not been processed and sought direction to respondent No.1 for taking decision at the earliest by referring his claim.

7. In the aforementioned facts of the case instead of keeping this writ petition pending seeking reply from the respondents, without commenting anything on merits of claim of petitioner, this writ petition at this stage is disposed of directing respondent No.1/ Collector to take decision on the application submitted by the petitioner under Section 64 of the Act of 2013 in accordance with law expeditiously,
preferably within a period of three months from the date of receipt of copy of order if already not decided/ order passed till date.

8. With the aforementioned observation and direction writ petition stands disposed of.
